name: Variables, memory & references
description: How variables name values in memory, and how references let two names point at the same object.
key_points: a variable is a name bound to a value in memory
assignment of an object copies the reference, not the object
two references can point to the same object, so mutation through one is visible through the other
passing an object to a function passes a reference

name: Arrays & indexing
description: Contiguous blocks of memory with constant-time access by index.
key_points: elements are stored contiguously in memory
indices start at 0 and the last index is n-1
access by index is O(1) using address arithmetic
inserting or deleting in the middle or front shifts elements and is O(n)

name: Big-O complexity
description: Describing how running time or memory grows with input size, ignoring constant factors.
key_points: big-O describes growth rate as input size grows
constant factors and lower-order terms are dropped
halving the input each step gives O(log n)
nested loops over the input usually give O(n^2)

name: Recursion: base case & recursive case
description: A function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version, stopping at a base case.
key_points: a recursive function calls itself on a smaller subproblem
the base case stops the recursion and returns directly
without a base case recursion never stops and overflows the stack
each recursive call must make progress toward the base case

name: Recursion & the call stack
description: Each function call gets its own stack frame holding its parameters and local variables.
key_points: each call pushes a new stack frame
every frame has its own copy of parameters and local variables
when a call returns its frame is popped and the caller resumes
deep recursion can cause a stack overflow

name: Linked lists
description: A chain of nodes where each node stores a value and a reference to the next node.
key_points: each node stores a value and a reference to the next node
access to the k-th element requires walking from the head, O(k)
insert or delete at a known node is O(1) by relinking pointers
deleting a node requires updating the previous node's next pointer

name: Stacks
description: A last-in, first-out (LIFO) collection supporting push and pop.
key_points: a stack is last-in first-out (LIFO)
push adds to the top and pop removes from the top
push and pop are O(1)
popping an empty stack is an underflow error that must be checked

name: Queues
description: A first-in, first-out (FIFO) collection supporting enqueue at the back and dequeue at the front.
key_points: a queue is first-in first-out (FIFO)
enqueue adds at the back and dequeue removes from the front
a circular buffer or linked list gives O(1) enqueue and dequeue
queues model waiting lines and breadth-first processing

name: Hash functions
description: Functions that map keys to array indices quickly and deterministically.
key_points: a hash function maps a key to an integer index
a hash function must be deterministic: same key, same hash
collisions are unavoidable when there are more keys than slots
a good hash function spreads keys uniformly

name: Hash tables & collisions
description: Arrays of buckets indexed by hash, with a strategy for handling collisions.
key_points: a hash table stores entries in buckets chosen by the hash
a collision means two keys map to the same bucket, not that the table is full
chaining or open addressing resolves collisions
average lookup is O(1) but worst case is O(n)
resizing keeps the load factor low

name: Tree terminology
description: Root, parent, child, leaf, depth and height in hierarchical node structures.
key_points: a tree has one root and every other node has exactly one parent
a leaf is a node with no children
depth is the number of edges from the root to a node
height is the number of edges on the longest path from a node down to a leaf

name: Binary trees
description: Trees where each node has at most two children: left and right.
key_points: each node has at most two children, left and right
height ranges from about log2 n (balanced) to n-1 (a chain)
a full or complete tree is a special case, not the rule
many algorithms process the left and right subtrees recursively

name: Pre/in/post-order traversal
description: Systematic recursive orders for visiting every node of a binary tree.
key_points: pre-order visits node, then left subtree, then right subtree
in-order visits left subtree, node, then right subtree
post-order visits left subtree, right subtree, then node
in-order traversal of a BST produces keys in sorted order

name: BST ordering property
description: Every key in a node's left subtree is smaller and every key in its right subtree is larger.
key_points: every key in the left subtree is less than the node
every key in the right subtree is greater than the node
the property applies to entire subtrees, not just direct children
the BST property says nothing about balance

name: BST search & insert
description: Searching and inserting by comparing keys and going left or right.
key_points: compare the key with the node and go left if smaller, right if larger
search and insert take O(h) where h is the tree height
a recursive search needs a base case for an empty (null) subtree
insertion adds the new key as a leaf where the search fell off the tree

name: BST deletion
description: Removing a key while keeping the BST property: leaf, one-child and two-child cases.
key_points: deleting a leaf just removes it
a node with one child is replaced by that child
a node with two children is replaced by its in-order successor or predecessor
the in-order successor is the leftmost node of the right subtree

name: Binary heaps
description: Complete binary trees stored in arrays where each parent is ordered relative to its children.
key_points: in a min-heap every parent is less than or equal to its children
a heap is only partially ordered, not sorted
a heap is a complete tree stored in an array with children at 2i+1 and 2i+2
insert and extract-min are O(log n) using sift-up and sift-down

name: Priority queues
description: Collections that always remove the highest-priority item first.
key_points: a priority queue removes the highest-priority item first, not the oldest
a binary heap gives O(log n) insert and remove
a sorted array gives O(1) remove but O(n) insert
priority queues power schedulers and Dijkstra's algorithm

name: Graph representation
description: Vertices and edges stored as adjacency lists or adjacency matrices.
key_points: a graph is a set of vertices connected by edges
an adjacency matrix uses O(V^2) space and gives O(1) edge lookup
an adjacency list uses O(V+E) space and suits sparse graphs
in an undirected adjacency list each edge appears twice

name: Breadth-first search
description: Exploring a graph level by level using a queue.
key_points: BFS uses a queue to explore nodes level by level
BFS marks nodes visited to avoid revisiting them
BFS finds shortest paths by number of edges in unweighted graphs
BFS runs in O(V+E) with adjacency lists

name: Depth-first search
description: Exploring a graph by going as deep as possible before backtracking, using a stack or recursion.
key_points: DFS goes as deep as possible before backtracking
DFS uses a stack or the call stack via recursion
DFS needs a visited set to terminate on graphs with cycles
DFS runs in O(V+E) with adjacency lists
